entries.effect: the value the caller set is HELD and READ BACK: a set of trusts under a lock, compared by value, and a NULL trust is errSecParam. WHAT THE RELEASE DOES WITH IT IS NOTHING, and that is the part a caller has to know: 6.1.3 resolves a trust against the anchors it was given and NEVER fetches a missing intermediate, so setting the flag and evaluating gives a verdict computed WITHOUT the fetched chain - on a chain that needs one that is a FAILURE, not a slower success
entries.reason: iOS 7.0, one release after 6.1.3, and the release has no earlier spelling of it and no other SecTrust function that sets a network-fetch flag, so there is nothing to delegate to; the port holds and reads back what the caller set, which is what inert means

entries.effect: the constant is the string sync, the key of the attribute; an item added with it true or false is kept on this device only, and a query that names it, true, false or Any, finds the items of the device whichever it names
entries.reason: a departure from 7.0 in what the keychain does with it: the keychain of iOS 6 takes the key and ignores it, and there is no iCloud Keychain to carry an item anywhere
